slides.0.title: Oregon III: the south, Columbia Gorge and cross-state AVAs
slides.0.subtitle: Southern Oregon, the Gorge, Walla Walla and the Columbia Valley
slides.1.title: Southern Oregon
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Parent and sub-AVAs
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The Southern Oregon AVA was approved in 2004 and contains the Umpqua Valley (1984), Rogue Valley (1991), Applegate Valley, Red Hill Douglas County (2005) and Elkton Oregon (2013)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Climate
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Mediterranean-influenced rather than maritime: hot, dry summers, with cooler nights at elevation
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Varieties
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Tempranillo is the flagship (Abacela was founded in 1995); Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon and Viognier also matter; Pinot Noir is grown mainly at higher or cooler western sites
slides.1.content: Southern Oregon is more like inland California: varied and showing character through Tempranillo and Syrah.
slides.2.title: Columbia Gorge: a cross-state rainfall gradient
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Extent
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Approved 10 May 2004; spans Oregon (Hood River, Wasco) and Washington (Skamania, Klickitat); about 179,200 acres, with about 1,300 planted
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Fast drying from west to east
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Rainfall drops by about an inch per mile: about 36 inches near Hood River and about 10 near Lyle, Washington
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Varied grapes
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Zinfandel, Riesling, Syrah and more, marketed as "a world of wine in 40 miles"
slides.2.content: The Gorge changes climate fast over short distances, so varieties range from cool to warm.
slides.3.title: Walla Walla and the Columbia Valley: shown in both states
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Walla Walla Valley
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Approved 6 February 1984; about 182,060 acres; in southeast Washington and the northeastern corner of Oregon
slides.3.highlights.1.title: The Rocks District
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Approved in February 2015 in Umatilla County, Oregon (Milton-Freewater) as a sub-AVA of Walla Walla; conventionally known for basalt cobble soils and Syrah
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Columbia Valley
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Approved 13 December 1984, mostly in Washington and extending into northern Oregon south of the Columbia River
slides.3.content: In this course's map and lessons, cross-state AVAs appear on both the Oregon and Washington sides and are marked as cross-state.
Which variety is Southern Oregon's flagship?
In which year was the Columbia Gorge AVA approved?
In which state is The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater?
Which AVA covers both Washington and Oregon?
Walla Walla Valley (so are the Columbia Valley and Columbia Gorge).
